To: docs/climate-programme/border-revenues-launch/handover
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT — Thursday launch handover for Inês

Inês,

I am taking the train tonight. My father is ill, I am with my family. I don’t yet know how long I will be away, so please plan to lead Thursday without me.

I am sorry. Finding the figure 3 error this afternoon and leaving you with the slides, the press correction and the launch is a real mess to hand over. The 2.1 mistake is mine, not yours. Please say that if anyone asks; you do not need to absorb responsibility for it because you are the person standing at the front.

I trust you completely. You know this paper as well as I do, and you ran the annex B sensitivity work yourself. You do not need to perform my version of the presentation or wait for my permission on every decision. Below is the order I would tackle things in.

This page is a draft for me to read on the train before sharing.

1. First priority: get the correction moving with Hanna

The correct estimate for 2030 LDC-relevant revenue is EUR 1.4 billion, not EUR 2.1 billion. Figure 3 and the summary had the estimate from the old run, which did not apply the free allocation phase-out. The conclusion of the paper does not change, but the headline number does. We should be clear about both parts, without making the correction sound smaller than it is.

PDF v7 on the drive is already corrected on pages 3, 14 and 15. The outstanding corrections are:
- Deck v4: slides 6 and 9, including any references in the speaker notes.
- The embargoed press release Hanna sent on Friday, which still says 2.1.

Please contact Hanna first so the press correction is not waiting behind slide polishing. The release went to 34 Brussels contacts and the embargo lifts Thursday 26 November at 10:00 CET. Ask her to send an explicitly labelled corrected release to everyone who received the original, with PDF v7, and make the replacement number unmistakable. Quietly replacing an attachment is not enough.

A usable correction line is:

“We have corrected the 2030 LDC-relevant revenue estimate from EUR 2.1 billion to EUR 1.4 billion. The earlier figure came from an old model run that did not apply the free allocation phase-out. The paper’s conclusion is unchanged; the corrected estimate is in PDF v7.”

Geert knows I am away. If Hanna needs a senior name to sign off the corrected release, he can do that. Please route it to him rather than wait for me. Check with Hanna that the correction has actually gone out before the embargo lifts, and that any public release or download uses the corrected material.

2. Next: make one clean presentation version

Use PDF v7 as the reference and correct slides 6 and 9 in deck v4. Slide 9 is the revenue chart. Check the chart, labels, headline text and speaker notes for the old number, then do a quick search through the whole deck for other references to 2.1. Save a clearly labelled corrected version so nobody picks up the wrong deck on Thursday.

The deck has 14 slides, but the speaking slot is now 15 minutes, not 20. Please cut whatever you need to cut. The revised timing is in Tomás’s Monday email, not the original run of show. I would protect the main finding, the corrected revenue estimate and the policy implications, and keep the detailed sensitivity discussion ready for questions rather than trying to fit everything into the talk.

You know which slides you can speak to without notes. Use your own words.

3. Confirm the event changes and access arrangements

Please tell Tomás that you are replacing me for both the presentation and the panel, and ask him to update the programme and introduce you accordingly.

The current timing is:
- 12:00: guests at the security entrance; Tomás handles badge collection. Light lunch outside the room from 12:00.
- 12:30: Lindqvist’s welcome, five minutes.
- 12:35: your presentation, 15 minutes.
- 12:50: panel starts.
- Before 13:30: Lindqvist wants to take at least two questions herself.
- 13:30: Lindqvist must leave for a vote.
- 14:00: close, unless the office confirms another change.

The original run of show puts Q&A at 13:40, so that part cannot simply stand unchanged. Ask Tomás to confirm how they want to bring questions forward and who moderates after Lindqvist leaves. We should not invent that arrangement on her behalf.

Final names from our side must reach Tomás by Wednesday 25 November at 12:00 latest; he says security will not admit people otherwise. Make sure your name is on the list and confirm everyone else who is actually coming. The venue is the European Parliament, Altiero Spinelli building, in the room booked by Lindqvist’s office.

4. Wednesday press calls: settle these with Hanna

Hanna promised two journalists a Wednesday afternoon call: one from a trade newsletter and one from a Belgian daily. The calendar holds 14:00 and 15:00 on Wednesday 25 November, 20 minutes each, but these are still marked “Hanna to confirm”.

Ask Hanna to confirm the callers, times and whether you are taking them. If the preparation load is too much, agree another arrangement with her rather than treating those slots as immovable. Either way, the journalists should have the corrected release and PDF before the conversation.

Lead with what the paper finds, explain the correction plainly, and distinguish the corrected estimate from the unchanged conclusion. If asked whose error it was: it was mine.

5. Panel preparation: do not let Kessler choose the whole conversation

Kessler has already said he will raise the 80% pass-through assumption and resource shuffling. Be ready, but do not let his opening turn the launch into a debate solely about his preferred parameter.

On pass-through, the straightforward answer is:
- 80% is the central case, not a claim that every manufacturer can pass through that much.
- Annex B tests 60% and 40%.
- The result holds at 60% and weakens at 40%.

Say the last point openly. There is no need to defend a stronger claim than the paper makes. You ran these sensitivities; you are the right person to explain them. Answer his point, then bring the discussion back to the paper’s findings and the LDC implications.

On resource shuffling: we agree it is a risk. Section 5.2 addresses it, and we recommend the Commission’s monitoring report. Do not get drawn into pretending we dismiss the concern.

Abena is joining remotely. Her link is in the calendar invite; the deck notes say she tested it successfully. Please let her know you are taking my place and arrange a brief sound/link check with whoever is handling the room. She was strong on the LDC issues on our call, but don’t assume she will answer any particular point for us.

And remember Lisbon: when the projector died at the COP side event, you rescued my panel. You are better live than you think. A difficult question or a technical hiccup does not mean you have lost the room.

6. Small but important follow-up

Lucy Tran is attending with a colleague. For the Halvorsen grant report she needs two event photos and the attendance numbers, ideally by 4 December. Before Thursday, agree who will take the photos and who will capture the attendance count, so this does not become another thing you have to reconstruct afterwards. Check access arrangements for Lucy and her colleague with the office as needed.

After the event, keep the final deck, corrected release, attendance figure and photos together in the launch folder. A short note of press follow-up or questions that need an answer would also help when I am back.

Reaching me

You can call me. After 9 tomorrow morning I might not pick up, so please do not make the correction or event decisions dependent on reaching me. Use Geert for the senior press sign-off if needed, Hanna for press arrangements and Tomás for the parliamentary logistics.

If anyone asks about my absence, all I want shared is: “My father is ill, I am with my family.” Nothing more.

I wish I were leaving you a clean deck and a quiet final few days. I am sorry that I am not. But I am not worried about whether you can lead this: I know you can. Thank you for taking it on.

Marieke
